Tang and Steckmann gave such a learner with polynomially many copies and $2^t$ times polynomial time when the noise strength is below a threshold of at most about $0.16$, which tends to zero as $t/n\to1$. They asked whether other algorithms with these resources can exceed this threshold. We answer this question affirmatively for every fixed bound on global depolarizing noise below one and every $0\le t\le n$, including states with only one promised independent stabilizer. Our learner uses polynomially many copies and $2^t$ times polynomial classical running time. All resource bounds hold on every execution. Their polynomial factors depend on $n,1/\varepsilon,\log(1/δ)$, with degrees and constants depending on the fixed noise promise.

papers.title: Computational Bounds for $f$-Routing
papers.abstract: The $f$-routing protocol is a leading candidate for quantum position verification (Kent, Munro, and Spiller, Physical Review A, 2011), but security guarantees for explicit functions remain limited. We prove unconditional resource lower bounds for uniform attackers. Our techniques bypass communication-complexity bounds central to previous works, which are inherently at most linear in the input length. We show that, for input length $n$ and a sufficiently small constant $ε>0$, a uniform strategy running in time $T$ and succeeding with probability at least $1-ε$ on every input implies the following computational bounds on $f$. 1. If the strategies are arbitrary quantum channels, then $f\in \mathrm{QSZK}(\mathrm{poly}(T))$, where $\mathrm{QSZK}(T)$ is the class of languages having quantum statistical zero-knowledge proofs in which the verifier runs in time $T$ and the simulator in time $\mathrm{poly}(T)$. 2. If the strategies are Clifford+T circuits using at most $t$ magic gates, then $f\in \mathrm{DTIME}(\mathrm{poly}(T2^t))$. 3. If the strategies are explicit Pauli-sparse unitaries acting on at most $T$ qubits and having at most $s$ nonzero Pauli coefficients, then $f\in \mathrm{DTIME}(\mathrm{poly}(Ts))$. Time and space hierarchies then yield explicit functions secure against superlinear and even all polynomial-time adversaries under our computational restrictions. These bounds exceed the bounded-storage qubit bound $q\leq\log n$ of Bluhm, Christandl, and Speelman (Nature Physics, 2022) for the inner product function $f=\mathrm{IP}$, at the cost of restricting adversarial computation and increasing honest evaluation complexity.

papers.title: Functional Dimensional Regularization for the Lee-Yang Model
papers.abstract: We apply functional dimensional regularization (FDR) to the Lee-Yang universality class, a paradigmatic non-unitary theory, and compute its main critical exponents across the dimension range $3\leq d\leq 6$. By combining a second-order derivative expansion with polynomial field expansions, we obtain results that are compatible with resummed $\varepsilon$-expansion as well as with state-of-the-art estimates from Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy Sphere techniques. This demonstrates that, in the context of non-unitary theories, FDR retains the efficiency and rapid convergence to accurate critical exponents already observed in the Ising and O(N) cases.

papers.title: Pervasive Vulnerability Analysis and Defense for QKD-based Quantum Private Query
papers.abstract: Quantum Private Query (QPQ) based on Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is among the most practically viable quantum communication protocols, with application value second only to QKD itself. However, prevalent security vulnerabilities in the post-processing stages of most existing QKD-based QPQ protocols have been severely overlooked. This study focuses on hidden information extraction under undetermined signal bits, revealing that most such QPQ protocols face severe security threats even without complex quantum resources. Specifically, direct observation attack causes incremental information leakage, while the minimum error discrimination attack efficiently steals additional database inforamtion. To address these critical flaws, the proposed multi-encryption defense scheme is compatible with existing QPQ protocols. The study demonstrates the necessity of the multi-encryption strategy for the security of databases in QPQ, providing key theoretical and technical support for constructing practical QPQ protocols resistant to real-world attacks.

papers.title: Inline inter-core phase control in multi-core fiber with a commercial polarization controller
papers.abstract: Inter-core phase control is a prerequisite for interferometry in multi-core fiber (MCF), but no compact inline element for this purpose is presently available, and existing approaches require fanout to single-mode fiber or free-space optics. We show that a commercial inline polarization controller, a low-loss and widely available component, can be operated as an inline inter-core phase shifter. Two-core interferometry on a jacketed four-core patchcord gives a reversible inter-core phase of $0.95 \pm 0.02$~rad from a single device, with an operating-point-independent lower bound of $0.38$~rad, driven through repeated load-unload cycles at a rate set by the actuator. A diametrically compressed disk model is used to predict the operating condition: with the input polarization aligned to a principal stress axis the device imparts a relative phase between cores without rotating the polarization state of either, which we verify by polarimetry on all four cores. The response is polarization dependent, falling to less than $0.58$~rad for the orthogonal input. The result is a practical, inline route to inter-core phase control and stabilization in all-MCF interferometers, requiring neither fanout to single-mode fiber nor free-space optics.

papers.title: Gauge-invariant quantum gravitational corrections to correlation functions
papers.abstract: A recent proposal for gauge-invariant observables in inflation [R. Brunetti et al., JHEP 1608 (2016) 032] is examined. We give a generalisation of their construction to general background spacetimes. In flat space, we calculate one-loop graviton corrections to a scalar two-point function in a general gauge for the graviton. We explicitely show how the gauge-dependent terms cancel between the usual self-energy contributions and the additional corrections inherent in these observables. The one-loop corrections have the expected functional form, contrary to another recently studied proposal for gauge-invariant observables [M. B. Fröb, Class. Quant. Grav. 35 (2018) 035005] where this is not the case. Furthermore, we determine the one-loop graviton corrections to the four-point coupling of the gauge-invariant scalar field, and the corresponding running of the coupling constant induced by graviton loops. Interestingly, the $β$ function is negative for most values of the non-minimal coupling of the scalar field to curvature, including minimal and conformal coupling.

papers.title: Neural network approximation of regularized density functionals
papers.abstract: We study neural-network approximation of density functionals in a Banach-space setting. Since the exact continuum functionals are discontinuous in the natural density topology, we apply $p$-Moreau-Yosida regularization. We construct finite-rank ReLU networks that preserve convexity and nonnegativity, lie below the regularized functional, and approximate it uniformly on compact sets. For energies obtained by minimization over compact density sets, we account exactly for the energy shift caused by regularization and bound the remaining error by the localization on these compact sets and network approximation errors. We apply this framework to canonical and grand-canonical density-functional theory at fixed particle number and fixed mean particle number, respectively. We obtain uniform energy convergence on norm-compact classes of external potentials, including molecular Coulomb potentials. We illustrate our results through numerical experiments on a simple model system.

papers.title: From photons to fractons: Casimir effect in higher-rank electrodynamics and its fractonic branch
papers.abstract: The Casimir effect probes the modes that can propagate between boundaries. This makes it useful for fracton gauge theories, where restricted mobility follows from the simultaneous conservation of charge and dipole moment and changes the physical sector of the theory. We compare ordinary Maxwell electrodynamics with a Lorentz-covariant higher-rank theory of a symmetric tensor gauge field and with the scalar-charge fractonic branch selected from it by a preferred timelike background. The comparison shows why the distinction matters. In the full covariant theory, the Euclidean slab problem contains three independently propagating Maxwell-like modes and two coupled vector sectors that do not reduce to independent ordinary modes. Their boundary determinants are well defined, but a Lorentzian analysis shows that the vector sector has an unbounded Hamiltonian, so these determinants do not describe the vacuum energy of a stable fractonic phase. On the fractonic branch, the Gauss constraint removes that vector sector and leaves three stable massless modes: two transverse-traceless tensor modes and one scalar trace mode. For ideal reflectors, the physical Casimir energy is therefore 3/2 of the corresponding Maxwell result, for both equal and complementary boundary conditions. The calculation isolates the effect of the fractonic restriction on the radiative spectrum and clarifies which features of the full higher-rank boundary problem survive in the physical fracton sector.

papers.title: Flowing with Displacements and Tilts: Surface Operators in $O(N)$ Models
papers.abstract: Defect conformal field theories have special operators of protected dimension known as displacements and tilts. They arise due to the breaking of global symmetries by the defect and the normalisations of their two-point functions are characteristics of the defect. In the case of surface defects, these normalisations are related to some of the anomaly coefficients in the surface effective action. To study these operators and their flows between different defect renormalization group fixed points we present an elegant approach using conformal perturbation theory that easily reproduces the known examples from the critical Wilson-Fisher $O(N)$ model in $4-\varepsilon$ dimensions and allows us to construct new ones in other multiscalar theories. In all the systems that we study the flows are short and under full control, as is the change of the displacement and tilt normalizations. We point out some novel features like the existence of vortices when the defect conformal manifold is not simply connected. In addition to regular human labour, this work relied heavily on generative AI; see full disclosure in methodology section.

papers.title: On the Optimality of Gaussian Code-books for Signaling over a Two-Users Weak Gaussian Interference Channel
papers.abstract: This article establishes that the capacity region of the two-users weak Gaussian interference channel can be achieved using Gaussian codebooks. It is further shown that the upper concave envelope of the achievable rate region can be attained using at most two time-sharing phases. In one phase, both users transmit simultaneously, while in the second phase, when present, only one user is active. Furthermore, the boundary of the capacity region can be traversed continuously through incremental reallocations of power between the two messages transmitted by each user. Finally, it is proven that the Han-Kobayashi achievable rate region with single-letter Gaussian codebooks attains the optimal boundary of the capacity region.

papers.title: Geometric Mode Steering of the Quantum Mpemba Effect
papers.abstract: The slowest Liouvillian mode often bottlenecks the relaxation of an open quantum system to its steady state. Standard strategies circumvent this bottleneck by selecting special initial states or engineering the dissipator. Here we investigate this problem when the input and the subsequent dissipative generator are prescribed. We introduce a predissipative geometric steering protocol that reshapes a prescribed pure or mixed state before relaxation begins---coherent rotations interleaved with nonselective projective measurements---at a fixed Lindblad generator. By steering the state's Bloch direction along geodesic paths, the protocol suppresses its overlap with the slowest Liouvillian modes. The prepared state can then start farther from equilibrium yet relax faster, realizing the quantum Mpemba effect, as diagnosed by reduced slow-mode overlap and a larger initial distance to stationarity, with distance crossings for complex slow modes verified from the full dynamics. Our framework treats real and complex spectral gaps within a common mode-overlap description. We also quantify the state-side cost of this preparation through cumulative measurement-induced mixing and illustrate its tradeoff with fidelity for a mixed target. We demonstrate Mpemba acceleration in driven qubit and multiqubit systems and discuss the required operations in trapped-ion and superconducting platforms.

papers.title: Qyantram: A Transparent and Verifiable Quantum Computing Platform
papers.abstract: Most quantum circuit platforms focus on idealized circuit assembly and simulation, hiding hardware compilation, error identification, and variational model training behind black-box operations. QYANTRAM addresses this gap through an open platform comprising four subsystems, built around evidence-backed results and independent verification. Its staged compilation pipeline makes every transformation traceable, while the router publishes rejected SWAP candidates and their scores for transparent decision-making. Verification exploits inactive qubits remaining in the |0> state, reducing complexity from 2^N to 2^k for k active qubits. This mathematically exact reduction enables full pre-compilation verification on 127- and 156-qubit layouts, achieving approximately 10,000x speed-ups with execution times below one millisecond. The error identification engine exhaustively evaluates all Pauli error patterns without sampling, matching closed-form predictions within 2.8e-17. Its machine-learning engine achieves numerical agreement within 2.0e-15 of qiskit.quantum_info while training 25-50 times faster. The router introduces approximately 1.27x more SWAP gates than Qiskit's SABRE due to its omission of optimization, trading routing efficiency for complete decision transparency and traceability.

papers.title: R7-branes and AdS$_{\text{9}}$ solutions in type IIB
papers.abstract: We consider the recently found $\mathrm{AdS}_9$ backgrounds in type IIB supergravity. We start by reviewing the solutions in a more convenient set of coordinates, which allows us to explicitly compute a few relevant observables, including the holographic central charge. Subsequently, we study non-supersymmetric 7-brane configurations sourced by the IIB axio-dilaton. We find explicit analytic 7-brane solutions that possess the above $\mathrm{AdS}_9$ backgrounds as their near-horizon geometry. Finally, we discuss the relation of these 7-brane solutions to the R7 branes by imposing the reflection monodromy $τ\rightarrow -\bar τ$ in the transverse plane.

papers.title: Hierarchy of entanglement detection criteria for random high-dimensional states
papers.abstract: Entanglement is a cornerstone in quantum information science, yet detecting it efficiently remains a challenging task. Focusing on states with nonpositive partial transpose (NPT), we establish a hierarchy among entropy-based, majorization, realignment, and reduction criteria for Haar uniformly generated random states in finite dimensions, analyzing their performance based on rank and subsystem dimension. We prove lower bounds on the rank of mixed quantum states beyond which the realignment and entropic criteria fail to detect entanglement. We evaluate the relative effectiveness of the considered detection methods using three key indicators -- fraction of detected states, mean detectable entanglement, and minimum required entanglement. Our results provide insights into the entanglement thresholds needed for reliable detection, showing that, beyond a certain level of entanglement, all criteria become equally powerful for low-rank states, while a hierarchy emerges among the various criteria for moderate to high ranks. Intriguingly, the proposed ordering among the considered criteria in qubit-qudit systems is different from that in higher dimensions. Additionally, we establish that the detection efficiency is influenced by the asymmetry in the subsystem dimensions, by illustrating how the realignment criterion behaves more efficiently than other detection methods when the difference between the subsystem dimensions is small.

papers.title: Quantum circuit design via dynamic Pauli constraints
papers.abstract: We introduce the Motte model, a software-oriented model of quantum computation motivated by the practical constraints of near-term quantum hardware. In this model, gates are specified by constraints expressed in terms of Pauli observables, with each disjoint layer of gates accompanied by a pairwise or k-local quantum state tomography of the device. We prove that the model is equivalent to the coupling-graph-restricted circuit model, and hence universal for BQP, with only polynomial overhead: emulating a depth-D circuit on N qubits requires O(D^2 N log N) elementary operations. Because the gate applied at each step is fixed exactly by the tomographic report, this emulation is robust to both the sampling and readout noise of the tomography. The model formalizes an idiom shared by existing work that ranges from quantum imaginary time evolution for the study of quantum systems to the use of quantum computers for procedural generation in games. It therefore provides a natural interface for designing quantum software entirely in terms of physically observable quantities, relevant for the NISQ era and into fault-tolerance, with gate and decoherence noise lying outside the present scope.

papers.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
papers.abstract: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $χ= 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $τ= 1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.

papers.title: Dynamics of Fock states in traveling pulses
papers.abstract: The quantum state of a traveling light pulse can qualitatively change the excitation dynamics of a two-level atom. We investigate this dependence for coherent and Fock input states using a virtual-cavity formulation with matched input and output temporal profiles. Analytical treatment of the master equation and numerical simulations show that coherent pulses produce damped Rabi oscillations, whereas Fock pulses can exhibit a partial recovery of the oscillation amplitude in the trailing part of the pulse. We examine how coupling to an auxiliary temporal mode and radiative loss shape this recovery. We also establish a connection with stimulated Raman adiabatic passage through an exact many-photon dark state and derive the associated adiabaticity condition. The observed recovery occurs away from ideal dark-state following. These results distinguish transient recovery in traveling-pulse scattering from conventional cavity collapse and revival, and clarify the scope of an adiabatic-transfer interpretation.

papers.title: What crossing symmetry forbids just above $c=1$
papers.abstract: What does a unitary two-dimensional conformal field theory look like just above $c=1$? Using the numerical conformal bootstrap, we study the four-point function of a scalar Virasoro primary $φ$ such that no primary lighter than $φ$ appears in its operator product expansion with itself. Slightly above $c=1$, crossing symmetry excludes the interval $0.17\lesssimΔ_φ\lesssim1$, although the compact boson realizes every such $Δ_φ$ at $c=1$. Combining this exclusion with results from the modular bootstrap, we show that the lightest primary of a compact unitary conformal field theory at $c=1.0005$ or $1.001$ has dimension $Δ_{\rm gap}<0.17$. Further from $c=1$, the largest excluded central charge at fixed $Δ_φ$ has two sharp minima near $Δ_φ=1/2$ and $4/7$. At these values it lies within $2\times10^{-7}$ of $c=8/7$, where the $\mathbb{Z}_5$ parafermion and its charge-conjugation orbifold have scalars of exactly these dimensions.

papers.title: The quantum magic of top quarks
papers.abstract: In recent years, a growing community of researchers has been applying ideas from Quantum Information theory to high energy physics. Entanglement is one such quantity, but there are by now many others. This contribution will examine the property of ``magic" (also known as ``non-stabliserness") which, roughly speaking, measures whether quantum systems have a genuine computational advantage over their classical counterparts. We will review the origin of this concept, before describing recent applications in collider physics, including top quark production.

papers.title: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage
papers.abstract: Ground states of Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK)-type models are volume-law entangled, which makes them costly both for tensor networks and for quantum hardware simulations. Thus, it remains unclear where quantum hardware could outperform classical simulation of such models. In this work, we study a spin SYK-dot chain, in which q dense SYK dots of p qubits are joined by single ZZ bonds of strength K. The entanglement across any cut is then bounded by floor(p/2) ln 2 plus the inter-dot entanglement, and the two-qubit depth of one Trotter step is set by p alone. A resource estimate shows that a quantum advantage for the ground state could appear only for dots of about 15 to 21 qubits or more. There, a single Trotter step already requires two-qubit error rates of order 10^{-6}, beyond the reach of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. We test the assumptions of this estimate with an imaginary-time matrix product state (MPS) that applies each dot as one block. It agrees with exact diagonalisation at (p, q) = (6, 2). At (5, 2), a variational circuit with the same dot-plus-link layout comes within 3.6% of the exact energy, and noisy simulations show that its fidelity decays as assumed in the resource estimate. At (8, 5), i.e., N = 40 qubits, the energy converges at bond dimension chi = 768, far below the exact value 2^20, and the inter-dot entanglement stays small and is set mainly by K. Out-of-time-order correlators across the links decay on a time scale that shrinks rapidly with |K|. Thus, the dot size p and the inter-dot coupling K together set the entanglement of the chain, and with it where a quantum advantage could appear.

papers.title: Non-local Magic: closed-form solution and equivalence with magic of purification
papers.abstract: Non-local magic quantifies the non-stabilizerness beyond the local choice of basis. Its evaluation is a hard problem requiring optimization over local unitaries. Here, we show that for the log-stabilizer fidelity this optimization admits an exact closed-form analytic solution depending only on the Schmidt spectrum. We then address the open problem of non-stabilizerness of mixed states by introducing the magic of purification and show that it naturally induces a resource theory whose free states are the states with zero stabilizer entropy. For the log-stabilizer fidelity, the magic of purification admits a distance-based formulation in terms of the Uhlmann fidelity. We prove that non-local magic coincides with the minimum magic of purification along the unitary orbit of the reduced density operator. This framework introduces non-local magic as the relevant resource for non-trivial steering and the characterization of entangling and non-stabilizer resources in measurements. These results provide both an efficient analytical characterization and a mixed-state resource-theoretic interpretation of non-local magic.

papers.title: Elementary proofs of quantum lower bounds for element distinctness and k-sum
papers.abstract: We give elementary proofs of the $Ω(n^{2/3})$ quantum query lower bound for element distinctness and the $Ω(n^{k/(k+1)})$ lower bound for the $k$-sum problem, for fixed $k$ and sufficiently large groups. The proofs use only basic properties of quantum states and linear algebra, analyzing the differences of algorithm states on different inputs.

papers.title: Harnessing Mutual Coupling in Cell-Free mMIMO
papers.abstract: This letter investigates a cell-free massive MIMO system with $L$ access points (APs), each employing a small fixed-form-factor, uniform linear array of $N$ potentially closely spaced antennas. Utilizing multiport communication theory, we analyze the impact of mutual coupling on uplink and downlink spectral efficiency (SE) under various impedance-matching strategies. We compare two deployment regimes: ($i$) increasing $N$ while $L$ is kept fixed, and ($ii$) increasing $N$ while fixing the total antenna count $M = NL$. Numerical results show that, with a full matching network, mutual coupling itself becomes beneficial when an AP serves several user equipments, which is the typical operating regime of user-centric cell-free networks. Furthermore, with full matching, antenna densification can enhance SE or allow for a reduction in the number of APs without performance loss. Since full matching networks remain of manageable size in the small arrays of distributed APs, unlike in large centralized arrays, cell-free networks offer a natural setting for exploiting mutual coupling.

papers.title: Universality and Emergent Classicality in Krylov Space
papers.abstract: Krylov complexity grows linearly at late times for many systems. In this regime, we give a general spectral formula for the leading growth coefficients of Krylov complexity and its higher moments, without requiring detailed knowledge of the Lanczos coefficients. For states with a narrow energy distribution compared to the bandwidth, dynamics in the Krylov basis resembles motion along a classical trajectory. We demonstrate our results for the critical XY chain and double-scaled SYK. For the latter, we compute the leading late-time behavior of the chord-number moments through one-loop order.

papers.title: The Covering Radius of the Reed--Muller Code \texorpdfstring{$\RM(3,8)$}{RM(3,8)} is 56
papers.abstract: We prove that the covering radius of the third-order Reed--Muller code in eight variables is fifty-six. The proof separates even- and odd-weight inputs by moment-controlled slicing. On the even side, a transport invariant on quadratic-label stars and consistency of singleton restrictions give a compatible cubic correction. On the odd side, symmetry of the third moment yields a covariance-rank obstruction. Its rank-two exception is a quartic plus three points of a two-plane; the zero-second-moment case is a prescribed-point perturbation of a quintic. We prove that every such point perturbation has third-order nonlinearity at most fifty-five by a marked derivative identity and complete restriction-code covers. Consequently the maximum among exact-degree-eight functions is fifty-five. The structural reductions are proved analytically, and complete finite certificates verify the explicitly stated local covering and compatibility assertions. The matching lower bound follows from the published quartic relative radius.

papers.title: Entanglement in the Schwinger effect
papers.abstract: We analyze entanglement generated by the Schwinger effect using a mode-by-mode formalism for scalar and spinor QED in constant backgrounds. Starting from thermal initial states, we derive compact, closed-form results for bipartite entanglement between particle-antiparticle partners in terms of the Bogoliubov coefficients. For bosons, thermal fluctuations enhance production but suppress quantum correlations: the logarithmic negativity is nonzero only below a (mode-dependent) critical temperature $T_c$. At fixed $T$, entanglement appears only above a critical field $E_{\text{entang}}$. For fermions, we observe a qualitatively different pattern: the fermionic logarithmic negativity is non-vanishing at finite temperature, and is monotonically suppressed by thermal noise. As a function of the electric field, it is non-monotonic, featuring a temperature-independent optimal field strength $E_*$ and decreasing on both sides of the maximum. We give quantitative estimates for analog experiments, where our entanglement criteria convert directly into concrete temperature and electric field constraints. These findings identify realistic regimes where the quantum character of Schwinger physics may be tested in the laboratory.

papers.title: Exact holographic superfluid at the Bogomolny point: transport, large charge, and Rényi entropies
papers.abstract: The Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$, in the probe limit, is a standard holographic model of a strongly coupled superfluid, usually solved numerically. When the scalar mass saturates the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound and the quartic coupling takes the Bogomolny value, its condensed phase can be found in closed form on every static, uncharged AdS$_5$ background with maximally symmetric spatial sections. We prove that it is linearly stable, as is any nodeless probe-limit condensate in the standard quantization with a nonnegative quartic coupling and no superflow. On each slicing it answers a different question about the dual conformal field theory. On the planar black brane it is the superfluid at all temperatures below $T_c$: the superfluid fraction follows the Gorter-Casimir two-fluid law exactly, and the speed and the attenuation of sound are found in closed form. In global AdS$_5$ it describes a state of charge $Q$ on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$, arguably the lowest-energy one, and gives its scaling dimension in closed form at all $Q$, classically in the bulk. Its excitations include towers that the superfluid effective theory does not describe; they come from an infrared fixed point of the probe sector. The hyperbolic slicing gives in closed form a homogeneous hairy phase of the black holes that compute the charged Rényi entropies of a ball. Its condensate does not vanish at the entangling surface. When sourced by operators inserted there, the phase sets in at Rényi index exactly one at zero chemical potential, as found for a neutral scalar.

papers.title: Photonic Time-Delayed Quantum Extreme Learning Machine
papers.abstract: We propose and numerically simulate a photonic quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) based on non-linear interactions in a time-delay non-linear interferometer with photon-number-resolving detection. We theoretically demonstrate the QELM's computational capability by binary classification of the non-linear two moons benchmark. Analysis of the learned output weights and alternative quantum readouts shows that compact feature sets based on photon-number correlations preserve classification accuracy while potentially reducing measurement complexity. We further show that the QELM maintains its classification performance under the effect of losses by naturally redistributing the learned weights across a larger set of available features. These results highlight the potential of time-delay photonic implementation as an experimentally accessible QELM platform.

papers.title: Enforced Gaplessness by Combining Non-Anomalous Symmetries
papers.abstract: Symmetry-enforced gaplessness is a phenomenon in which a quantum system is forced to be gapless due to its global symmetry. Previous works have mainly focused on anomalous symmetries. Another approach, using symmetry spans, which specify two embeddings of a common symmetry into two larger symmetries, was proposed by the authors. In this work, we show that a symmetry span can enforce gaplessness even when both larger symmetries are invertible and non-anomalous: each alone admits a trivially gapped phase, but because the embeddings differ by a twist associated with a symmetry-protected topological phase, the symmetry they generate admits no gapped phase with finitely many ground states. We present such a span of a finite group and $\mathrm{U}(1)^2$ in 1+1 dimensions, with continuum realizations and a lattice Hamiltonian, with a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space and finitely many parameters, that is gapless in any region of its parameter space. We also discuss a 2+1-dimensional example and spans of only finite symmetries.

papers.title: Taming a macroscopic free mass through continuous quantum measurement
papers.abstract: The free particle is the most elementary dynamical system in quantum mechanics. Despite remarkable progress in quantum control of increasingly massive solid-state mechanical oscillators, the analogous control of the free-particle counterpart has remained elusive. Dissipation and environmental noise have prevented such control in the inherently low-frequency domain of free-particle dynamics---a regime of growing importance for quantum sensing and tests of fundamental physics. Here we realize a suspended 1-milligram rotor operating in the free-particle regime with exceptional environmental isolation. Combining this isolation with a low-noise measurement architecture, we directly resolve thermal fluctuations in the motion associated with a damping rate of only 7~nHz. Through continuous quantum measurement of the rotor, we localize its otherwise unconfined motion, obtaining conditional states with entropic temperatures as low as 140~nK as a quantitative measure of control in the free-particle regime. This is two orders of magnitude below temperatures previously achieved in tabletop optomechanical experiments. We demonstrate immediate utilities of the new operating regime, setting new constraints on modifications of quantum mechanics and benchmarking inferred entanglement-to-decoherence rate ratios nearly two orders of magnitude beyond the state of the art for tests of gravity at the quantum-classical interface.

papers.title: Correlated Catalysis Removes the Strong Converse for Entanglement Distillation
papers.abstract: Entanglement distillation converts noisy shared quantum states into maximally entangled pairs using local operations and classical communication. The distillable entanglement $E_D$ determines the maximum asymptotic rate at which this process can be performed reliably. For several classes of quantum states, distillation above this rate obeys a strong converse: the fidelity with the target state vanishes asymptotically. Here we show that correlated catalysis removes the strong converse for every distillable bipartite state. Specifically, at any target rate $R>E_D$, the optimal asymptotic fidelity is given by $E_D/R$. Thus, although catalysis does not increase the maximum reliable distillation rate, it allows nonvanishing fidelity at every finite rate. Remarkably, this advantage persists even when the catalyst is returned exactly at every finite blocklength and the correlations between the output and catalyst vanish asymptotically. We further characterize the catalyst size required to sustain nonvanishing fidelity above the reliable distillation rate.

papers.title: Non-Abelian Dirac oscillator in a uniform Yang--Mills background: spin--isospin mixing and singlet--triplet splitting
papers.abstract: We investigate a planar Dirac oscillator coupled to a spatially uniform \(\utwo=\uone\times\su\) Yang--Mills background. The gauge configuration, adapted from the Dossa--Avossevou construction, contains an Abelian magnetic field \(B\), a non-Abelian spatial amplitude \(β\), and a non-Abelian scalar amplitude \(ρ\). Within the Pauli-reduced formulation, the non-Abelian field strength produces a constant operator on \(\mathbb{C}^{2}_{\mathrm{spin}}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{2}_{\mathrm{iso}}\). This operator contains a diagonal internal-Zeeman contribution proportional to \(σ^{3}T^{3}\) and an off-diagonal spin--isospin term proportional to \(σ^{1}T^{1}+σ^{2}T^{2}\). Its diagonalization gives a doubly degenerate aligned branch and two mixed branches with eigenvalues \[ λ_{\mathrm{FM}}=\frac{g^{2}β^{2}}{4m},\qquad λ_{S}=-\frac{g^{2}β(β-2ρ)}{4m},\qquad λ_{T}=-\frac{g^{2}β(β+2ρ)}{4m}. \] Consequently, the aligned internal-Zeeman scale is quadratic in \(β\), whereas the singlet--triplet separation is linear in \(βρ\). The revised formulation makes the sign conventions explicit, verifies the main limiting cases, distinguishes the Pauli-reduced spectrum from a full first-order Dirac diagonalization, and clarifies the physical meaning of the numerical illustrations.

papers.title: Noise-robust discrimination of incoherent point sources with spatial-mode demultiplexing
papers.abstract: We theoretically predict and experimentally demonstrate that a reduced spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) measurement using only the two lowest-order Hermite-Gaussian modes exhibits remarkable robustness against background noise in discriminating between a single source and two incoherent point sources. We establish a theoretical framework incorporating uniform background noise and derive an analytical Chernoff exponent expression, showing that SPADE consistently outperforms direct imaging (DI) across all source separations. Experimental results confirm that SPADE-based hypothesis testing approaches the quantum limit even when the background-to-signal photon ratio per pixel is 0.11. This advantage stems from SPADE's ability to concentrate source information into minimal detection modes, reducing the cumulative background noise impact. Our findings provide a practical detection scheme for applications where background noise is inevitable, such as astronomical observations and quantum sensing.

papers.title: Reed-Muller Codes are Optimal Binary Linear 3-Query LCCs
papers.abstract: We prove that any linear $3$-query locally correctable code $C \colon \mathbb{F}_2^k \to \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with constant correction radius must have length $n \geq 2^{Ω(\sqrt{k})}$. This improves on the prior best lower bound of $2^{Ω(\sqrt{k/\log k})}$, due to [AG24], and shows that the folklore construction of linear $3$-LCCs from Reed-Muller codes, which achieve length $n = 2^{O(\sqrt{k})}$, is optimal up to constant factors in the exponent. Our proof builds on the approach of [KM24a], further refined in [Yan24,KM24b], that uses "chain derived equations" in combination with Kikuchi graphs. The crux of our argument is to show that a certain edge-coloured Kikuchi graph has a unique colour cycle: a cycle in which some colour is used exactly once. We do this by controlling the distribution of colours at each vertex in the graph using a random walk mixing argument and a novel hypergraph decomposition based on edge expansion of the hypergraph's "flattening" into a graph.

papers.title: Limits of Finite-Sample Dependence Measures under Data Processing Inequality
papers.abstract: We study dependence measures between two discrete random variables. The measures vanish at independence and satisfy the data processing inequality (DPI): stochastic post-processing of one variable cannot increase dependence. We ask which such measures admit an exactly unbiased estimator from a fixed finite number of i.i.d. samples, a property equivalent to being polynomial in the joint probabilities. We distinguish fixed-alphabet DPI, which preserves the alphabet size of the variable being processed, from dimension-changing DPI. Under one-sided fixed-alphabet DPI, every measure with a continuously differentiable extension to a neighborhood of the closed probability simplex vanishes whenever one processed state has zero probability. If the processed alphabet is larger than the other alphabet, the measure is identically zero. If it has $n$ states and the other alphabet has at least $n$, every nonzero polynomial measure has degree at least $2n$ and requires at least $2n$ samples for unbiased estimation. Both bounds are attained by the Gram determinant. Under one-sided dimension-changing DPI, every family with the same boundary regularity is identically zero. These results yield sharp task bounds for multi-task peer prediction. For two agents with $n$ signals each, $2n$ tasks are necessary and sufficient for nontrivial expected payments that vanish for independent reports and cannot increase under memoryless stochastic garbling. Under these requirements, unequal signal-space sizes force the larger-alphabet agent's expected payment to vanish identically for any finite number of tasks.

papers.title: Directional Codes for Quantum LDPC Error Correction on Square and Hexagonal Grid Architectures
papers.abstract: Utility-scale quantum computing requires quantum error correction (QEC) to protect quantum information against noise. Currently, superconducting hardware is a promising candidate for achieving fault tolerance due to its fast gate times and feasible scalability. However, it is often restricted to two-dimensional nearest-neighbour connectivity, and therefore the variety of quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes that can be implemented on it without sacrificing QEC performance is believed to be greatly restricted. In this paper we construct a new family of qLDPC codes, which we call ``directional codes'', that outperforms the rotated toric code (RTC) while satisfying the connectivity requirements of the widely adopted square-grid, and some even the sparser hexagonal-grid, on a torus. The key idea is to utilise the iSWAP gate -- a native gate demonstrated on superconducting qubits -- to construct circuits that measure the stabilisers of these qLDPC codes without the need for additional connections. We numerically evaluate the performance of directional codes, encoding four, six, twelve and eighteen logical qubits, using a common superconducting-inspired circuit-level Pauli noise model. We also compare them to the RTC and to the bivariate bicycle (BB) codes, currently the two most popular quantum LDPC code families. As a concrete example, when evaluated with the Tesseract decoder with short beam setting, the best directional code family investigated achieves the same logical error rate as the RTC at physical error rate $p=10^{-3}$ but requires only a quarter to a third of the number of physical qubits to encode a given number of logical qubits. Our discovery opens a novel direction in QEC code design, suggesting that complex high-connectivity hardware may not be necessary for low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation.

papers.title: On the regularity index of the minimum distance function in projective nested Cartesian codes
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a projective nested product of fields and let $δ_X(d)$ be the minimum distance in degree $d\geq 1$ of the projective nested Cartesian code $C_X(d)$. The regularity index ${\rm reg}(δ_X)$ of the minimum distance function $δ_X$ is the minimum integer $d_0\geq 0$ such that $δ_X(d)=1$ for $d\geq d_0$. We give a formula for ${\rm reg}(δ_X)$ by determining an indicator function of least degree for each point of $X$ and using the fact that ${\rm reg}(δ_X)$ is the ${\rm v}$-number of the vanishing ideal $I_X$ of $X$. Then we give an arithmetical criterion that characterizes when $X$ is Cayley--Bacharach.

papers.title: Belief Propagation-Informed Tesseract Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: In quantum error correction, the decoder must estimate the errors from the measurement data accurately and fast enough to avoid a backlog. Search-based decoders such as Tesseract achieve high accuracy by finding a minimum-weight set of error events with an A* search, but their search effort grows rapidly with the physical error rate and the code size. To reduce this search effort while maintaining a logical error rate close to that of Tesseract, we propose a belief propagation (BP)-guided modification of the Tesseract decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. Damped sum-product BP is applied to the triggered detectors before the Tesseract search. If the detectors triggered by the BP hard decision match the triggered detectors, this hard decision is accepted directly, and the Tesseract search is skipped. Otherwise, the BP marginal probability estimates, weighted by a trust coefficient, modify the search priority, while the path cost keeps the channel-prior weights so that the decoding objective is unchanged. The framework also supports BP-based initialization, in which selected BP decisions form the starting point of a residual search whose signed-cost objective allows incorrect initial decisions to be removed. A node-exploration limit bounds this residual search; if the limit is reached, the decoder falls back to the BP-guided search on the original triggered detector set. The method is evaluated on the [[72,12,6]], [[90,8,10]], and [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle codes under circuit-level noise. With BP-based initialization and a global trust coefficient, the number of Tesseract search nodes expanded is reduced by up to more than two orders of magnitude at low physical error rates, while the logical error rate remains close to that of Tesseract.

papers.title: Discrepancy for Random Linear Codes
papers.abstract: We show that random linear codes (RLCs) possess nearly optimal discrepancy-type properties in a broad range of settings. Our main results are two general discrepancy theorems: one controls all translates of a fixed test, and the other controls large families of Fourier-pseudorandom tests. Two motivating examples follow: First, RLCs behave essentially like unstructured random codes for list-decoding from errors above capacity. More precisely, an RLC $C\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of rate $1 - \frac{1}{n}\log_q|B_ρ| + \varepsilon$, where $|B_ρ|$ is the volume of a radius-$ρ$ Hamming ball in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, satisfies $|C \cap B| = (1\pm o(1)) \frac{|C|\cdot |B|}{q^n}$ simultaneously for all radius-$ρ$ Hamming balls $B$ with high probability. This significantly strengthens the best prior results, which follow from work by Blinovsky (1987, 1990) and Levitin (1988) on the covering properties of RLCs. Second, over prime fields, RLCs behave essentially like unstructured random codes for zero-error list-recovery, and list-recovery from erasures, above capacity. More precisely, for a prime $q>2$ and input list size $2\leq \ell\leq q-1$, an RLC $C\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of rate $1-\log_q \ell+\varepsilon$ will satisfy $|C \cap S| = (1\pm o(1)) \frac{|C|\cdot \ell^n}{q^n}$ simultaneously for all combinatorial rectangles $S=S_1\times S_2\times\cdots\times S_n$, where $|S_i|=\ell$ for all $i$, with high probability. An analogous result also holds when we can bound $|S_i|$ only for some of the $i$'s. We use this to show the abundance of locally leakage-resilient $n$-party linear ramp secret sharing schemes with any linear reconstruction threshold and sublinear threshold gap $O(n/\log n)$ over fields of polynomial size $q=Θ(n^γ)$ for a constant $γ\in(0,1/5)$. Prior work was stuck at reconstruction thresholds above $n/2$ for both threshold and ramp schemes.

papers.title: The use of Peres lattices in periodically driven systems
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the strength of the method of Peres lattices in periodically driven quantum systems. The method, which has previously been used mostly in stationary systems, enables us to efficiently detect resonances in the driven system, to monitor the onset of chaos, and to recognize critical properties of the Floquet modes. It also allows quick comparisons of the spectra of Floquet modes for various driving Hamiltonians and transparent tests of the iterative approximation techniques based on effective stationary Hamiltonians.

papers.title: Many-Body Correlations in Phase-Space Microscopes
papers.abstract: The recently proposed "phase-space microscope" (PSM) extends quantum gas microscopes by allowing joint, single-shot measurements of position and momentum. We show that the $n$-body correlation functions constructed from such phase-space snapshots determine, in principle, all $n$-body observables of a many-body quantum state. This establishes phase-space imaging as a complete probe of strongly correlated matter, beyond what snapshots of position and momentum can provide---a limitation that goes back to a famous question posed by Pauli. Even without the full reconstruction of the density matrices, the PSM provides valuable insight into the quantum states. We demonstrate this power through several applications: witnessing entanglement hidden from both position and momentum, including between spatially separated collective degrees of freedom; resolving pairing structure across the BEC-BCS crossover, including the phase of the pair wavefunction and the reconstruction of its two-body Wigner function; probing inhomogeneous systems and preformed pairs without long-range order, relevant to the pseudogap phase; extracting the interaction energy in a magnetic field; and measurements of the local Chern marker. Furthermore, we discuss phase imprinting in the matter-wave Fourier plane as an alternative method for probing time-reversal-symmetry-broken phases such as chiral $p$-wave superconductors. Together, these results establish the PSM as a versatile new tool for exploring fundamental features of quantum many-body phases in strongly correlated quantum matter.

papers.title: On physical origin of Berry connection of free relativistic electrons
papers.abstract: No consensus has been reached on the appropriate operators for the spin and orbital angular momentum of free relativistic electrons. But there is a tendency to believe the existence of a spin-orbit coupling through the Berry connection. Here we show that this is not the case. Because the positive-energy solution of the Dirac equation is associated with the state of the electron, it is reasonable to postulate that only when projected onto the positive-energy subspace can observable operators on the Hilbert space of the Dirac equation represent physical quantities of the electron. On this basis, we find, after mapping the projected operators onto an irreducible representation, that the Berry connection describes the position of a quantum reference point with respect to the laboratory reference frame, relative to which the position of the electron is canonical. The orbital angular momentum of the quantum reference point about the origin of the laboratory reference frame is expressed in terms of the Berry connection. It combines with the canonical orbital angular momentum of the electron about the quantum reference point to give the orbital angular momentum of the electron about the origin of the laboratory reference frame.

papers.title: Second-order mean force Gibbs state of fermionic open systems
papers.abstract: Thermodynamics typically assumes that a system in contact with a thermal reservoir relaxes to the Gibbs state, or to the grand canonical Gibbs state when it also exchanges particles. However, this only holds when the coupling is very weak. Beyond this, the expected equilibrium state is the mean force Gibbs (MFG) state, obtained by tracing the reservoir out of the thermal state of the combined system. Despite its relevance, general analytic results for the MFG state have so far been obtained almost exclusively for bosonic reservoirs. Here we derive the grand canonical MFG state to second order in the coupling for a generic fermionic system coupled to a thermal reservoir at arbitrary chemical potential, using the concept of the mode reduced state in order for the fermionic MFG state to be well defined. The correction to the bare Gibbs state separates into particle and hole channels weighted by the empty and occupied reservoir states, related through the Kubo-Martin-Schwinger condition. We apply the result to the resonant level model, two modes coupled to a shared reservoir, and the single impurity Anderson model. For the two modes, the reservoir mediates coherence between modes that do not interact directly, something the bare Gibbs state cannot capture. We verify our results against numerically exact calculations, including real-time dynamics for the interacting model, and find agreement between the static prediction and the dynamical relaxation.

papers.title: Second-order evolution of spin shear tensor for massive spin-1/2 particles
papers.abstract: We present the second-order evolution equation for the spin shear component of the spin tensor in spin-polarized fluids, using a classical description of the spin degrees of freedom. Employing a semi-classical kinetic theory for the massive spin-1/2 particles within the relaxation time approximation we obtain a relaxation-type equation describing the evolution of spin shear driven by various thermodynamic forces and high-order gradient corrections. This equation yields a new set of transport coefficients that govern the dynamics of the dissipative spin-shear tensor.

papers.title: Spectral instability of charged scalar quasinormal modes and superradiance: Stabilizing the unstable
papers.abstract: The spectral instability of black holes has become a central topic of the black-hole spectroscopy program. Small changes to the black-hole scattering potential are known to produce disproportionately large migrations of its quasinormal modes in the complex plane, but it is unclear whether this sensitivity carries over to energy extraction through superradiance. We study this relation for massless charged scalar fields on Reissner--Nordström and Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter backgrounds. A localized positive potential bump, small in mass-scaled height, is displaced outward from the light ring while the original radiative boundary conditions are preserved. In the asymptotically flat case, a quasinormal branch enters the superradiant frequency regime while remaining damped. By searching for competing modes, we show that the least-damped positive-frequency mode also enters this regime, after a series of mode overtakings driven by quasinormal-mode migration. The real-frequency amplification, nevertheless, is only weakly affected and develops no pronounced narrow resonance. In de Sitter black holes, the bump can move an initially growing monopole mode into the damped half of the complex plane, stabilizing selected configurations that are initially modally unstable. After stabilization, the peak superradiant amplification can remain above both its unperturbed value and a gain of $100\%$; it falls below $100\%$ only for more distant bump locations. A prescribed positive perturbation can thus suppress modal growth without changing the superradiant frequency bounds or immediately suppressing the scattering peak.

papers.title: MPS overlaps and Sklyanin determinants
papers.abstract: We derive explicit overlap functions for integrable matrix product states associated with arbitrary finite-dimensional irreducible evaluation representations of the orthogonal and symplectic twisted Yangians. The central step is to relate the commuting quasi-determinants entering the universal overlap formula to Sklyanin determinants of nested subalgebras. For orthogonal evaluation representations, this relation determines their spectra directly in the Gelfand--Tsetlin basis. In the symplectic case, we combine Sklyanin determinants and minors with a factorization of the nested rank-two boundary matrices to obtain the corresponding spectra. The resulting overlap functions are explicit products parametrized by Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns and require only the highest-weight data of the underlying orthogonal or symplectic representation. Together with the universal ratio of Gaudin determinants and the model-dependent pseudovacuum overlap coefficients, they determine the normalized MPS overlaps. We also express the overlap functions in the orthogonal case beyond evaluation representations in terms of the highest weights arising along the nested twisted-Yangian subalgebras.

papers.title: Higher Groupoids of Gauge Potentials in Higher Gauge Theories admitting Weights
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit small model for the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances of higher gauge curvatures by algorithmically trivializing their nonlinear Bianchi identities. More precisely, for a finite-type Sullivan minimal Bianchi algebra equipped with positive integer weights, we organize weighted potentials and higher gauge parameters at each fixed curvature into an $\infty$-groupoid whose gauge transformations are linear in the parameters. We prove that this model is naturally equivalent to the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances through an intermediate total-form model, with explicit projection and section maps and simplicial homotopies. When nonempty, its connected components form a torsor for the degree-zero cohomology of an associated weighted gauge complex, and its higher homotopy groups are computed by the higher cohomology of this complex.

papers.title: Resilient Cell-Free MIMO ISAC Under Uncertainties: An Impairment-Aware Graph Neural Network Framework
papers.abstract: Beamforming designs for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in cell-free multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems face the challenge to stay reliable under uncertainties from both channel state information (CSI) as well as clutter. To this end, this paper proposes an impairment-aware heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) framework for beamforming that obtains the CSI error level and the clutter covariance as edge features, which enables a single trained model to adapt to both impairments. In particular, the GNN is trained on a low quantile of the minimum user rate with a clutter-aware signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio, balanced by a normalized Tchebycheff scalarization. Simulation results show that the proposed GNN framework outperforms the considered baselines in sensing-only and communication-only settings. Depending on the operating point, a single GNN model attains approximately 97\% of each baseline's rate while serving both functionalities at once. The model further generalizes to unseen CSI error levels and clutter counts and renders the ISAC system resilient.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for BD-RIS-Assisted Multi-UAV RSMA Communications
papers.abstract: Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs) extend conventional diagonal RISs by allowing controllable coupling among reflecting elements. This flexibility is attractive for aerial networks, where unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) face rapidly varying channels and strict power limits. In this paper, we study a hybrid BD-RIS-assisted multi-UAV rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) downlink, in which UAVs within favourable BD-RIS coverage use both direct and BD-RIS-aided links, whereas the remaining UAVs are served through direct links only. We formulate a network sum-rate maximization problem that jointly optimizes UAV trajectories, RSMA common-rate allocation, beamforming, BD-RIS scattering matrices, and UAV-BD-RIS association. The resulting mixed-integer non-convex problem is solved by using deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm, equipped with a constraint-preserving action layer that generates reciprocal and lossless BD-RIS responses in closed form and handles the binary association inside the environment transition. Simulation results, averaged over three training seeds under a physically consistent channel model with blocked direct links near the BD-RISs, show that the proposed design attains a sum rate comparable to SAC and higher than twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient ( TD3), proximal policy optimization (PPO), and deep Q-network (DQN), exceeds per-slot alternating optimization with fixed trajectories at about 1/65 of its per-slot runtime, and benefits mainly from RSMA, while the additional BD-RIS gain is modest.

papers.title: Hotplug Coded Caching: Uncoded versus Row-Wise Coded Placements
papers.abstract: In the hotplug coded caching model, $K$ users fill their caches of size $M$ as a function of $N$ files, but only an unknown subset of $A\leq K$ users is active in the delivery phase. In all regimes where the optimal hotplug tradeoff is known, it depends only on $A$, not on $K$; whether this holds in general is open. We show that: (i) Under uncoded placement, YMA delivery with MAN placement, where offline users are assigned the demands of active users, is optimal. Hence, offline users cause a strict load penalty at intermediate memory sizes, while the MAN placement is optimal for every number of active users; (ii) Under row-wise placement (RWP), where each cache is a function of the user's own row of each file, every classical scheme can be embedded in a Reed-Solomon code. The resulting hotplug scheme has the tradeoff of the classical model with $A$ users, for every $A\leq K$: there is no load penalty, but the placement depends on $K$. We then derive a converse for RWP, which shows that: (a) for $2\leq N\leq A$, the scheme of Gomez-Vilardebo (GV) is RWP optimal for $AM\leq N/(N-1)$, which settles the RWP tradeoff for $N=2$; (b) YMA is RWP optimal at $AM=N$; and (c) for $N=A=3$, GV is RWP optimal for $M\leq 1$. Hence, the Reed-Solomon embeddings of these schemes are optimal among embedded RWP schemes.

papers.title: Entanglement asymmetry in the gapped XYZ spin-$\frac12$ chain
papers.abstract: The entanglement asymmetry measures how strongly a symmetry is broken inside a subsystem. Analytic results at equilibrium have so far covered free theories and, perturbatively, the critical XXZ chain. We compute the Rényi entanglement asymmetries of a large interval in the gapped, $U(1)$-breaking phase of the interacting XYZ chain. The calculation combines three ingredients. A charged-moment identity, which we prove for fermionic Gaussian and for injective matrix-product ground states, ties the asymmetry to the static susceptibility of the broken charge. A non-conservation sum rule then evaluates the susceptibility from sine-Gordon form factors, its two-kink and one-breather channels providing a lower bound on the universal amplitude. The Baxter--Johnson--Krinsky--McCoy solution supplies the kink mass for different couplings. Infinite-system density-matrix renormalization group simulations built on these masses reproduce the master formula.

papers.title: A Survey on Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces: Fundamentals, Recent Advances, and Challenges
papers.abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) cascade several closely spaced programmable metasurface layers so that an electromagnetic wave undergoes repeated modulation-propagation interactions before leaving the stack. The stack thereby implements, at the speed of propagation and with few radio-frequency chains, high-dimensional analog transformations that would otherwise require digital precoding, combining, spatial filtering, focusing, or inference. Since 2023, SIM research has produced more than two hundred articles, a dedicated magazine special issue, and two survey-level overviews organized around applications and wave-domain computing. This article complements them with a model-to-hardware perspective. First, we present the electromagnetic modeling hierarchy of SIMs, making explicit the assumptions under which the models coincide, their validity regimes, and their computational complexity, with a common notation for hardware non-idealities and power consumption. Second, we present a methodology-first taxonomy (SIM-aware channel acquisition, model-based optimization, statistical-CSI design, learning-based control, and hardware-aware robust design), compare the families in terms of CSI requirements, complexity, convergence, and hardware constraints, and reconcile conflicting findings in the literature. Third, we synthesize applications by the physical role of the SIM. Fourth, we quantitatively compare experimentally demonstrated multilayer prototypes, separate validated from conceptual architectures, and discuss thermal, tolerance, and calibration issues. Fifth, we provide a tutorial-style performance and trade-off analysis anchored in reported results. Finally, we map evidence-based challenges to research directions with measurable targets. Lessons learned are summarized at the end of every section.

papers.title: Transgression branes in seven dimensions
papers.abstract: A seven dimensional theory with branes, described by a Transgression Action is investigated. The theory has special properties owing to the factorization of the trace used to define the Transgression form. It is shown that in some cases the theory is similar to the models of branes proposed by Nepomechie, Wu and Zee as a higher dimensional generalization of models of particles with fractional statistics of Wilczek, Wu and Zee. Static Euclidean solutions are presented, and compared with similar solutions of Nepomechie,Wu and Zee. Then Lorentzian static solutions are considered, based in solutions of constant curvature black holes presented by Bañados and further studied by Guilleminot, Olea and Petrov. Topological phases and their implications for quantum statistics are discussed.

papers.title: Entropy Bounds for Local Coordination and Graph Amenability
papers.abstract: We study local coordination on finite graphs, equivalently, the ability of randomized local protocols with independent private randomness to produce highly correlated outputs at neighboring vertices. Hutchcroft, Rospuskova, and Tamuz (2026) showed that if such local coordination can be achieved with low cost, then the graph admits a low-cost leader profile, or equivalently an appropriate bounded-radius decomposition, with a square-root loss in the cost. We substantially improve this bound for unbiased binary outputs. If the average disagreement is $\varepsilon$, we construct a leader profile of cost $O(\varepsilon\log(1/\varepsilon))$. The key ingredient is an information-theoretic influence measure: after fixing an ordering of the independent information sources, we assign to each binary output the increments of mutual information revealed along that ordering. For two outputs that disagree with probability $p$, the corresponding measures are within binary entropy $h(p)$ in total variation. Combined with a grand coupling theorem, this yields the improved bound. We also show that a universal linear bound is impossible. We construct graphs with binary local profiles of cost $O(\varepsilon)$ for which every leader profile has cost $$ Ω\!\left(\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}\right). $$ The construction uses weighted majority functions and can be implemented as an action-symmetric Nash equilibrium, giving a negative answer to the question of HRT whether leader equilibria are always optimal up to a constant factor. Finally, we show that the binary assumption is essential: for general real-valued outputs, the square-root dependence of the HRT theorem is sharp up to a universal constant.

papers.title: Low Overhead Universal Quantum Computation with Triorthogonal Codes
papers.abstract: We study the use of triorthogonal codes for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation and propose two methods to circumvent the Eastin-Knill theorem, which prohibits any single quantum error-correcting code from supporting both universality and a transversal gate set. We show that our methods reduce the resource overhead compared with existing fault-tolerant protocols. We develop a simple fault-tolerant implementation of the logical Hadamard gate for triorthogonal codes by exploiting the fact that they have transversal controlled-Z (CZ) gates, resulting in a circuit with reduced overhead. We also introduce a procedure for generating a symmetric Calderbank-Shor-Steane code paired with a triorthogonal code, which allows CNOT and CZ gate transversality across the pair of codes. In addition, we present logical state teleportation circuits that transfer encoded states between the two codes, allowing all logical operations to be performed transversally. Our methods can be integrated into the Steane error correction framework without incurring additional resource cost. Finally, using the 15-qubit code as an example, we demonstrate that our protocols significantly reduce the gate overhead compared with other existing methods. These results highlight the potential of combining distinct code structures to achieve low-overhead, universal fault-tolerant quantum computation.

papers.title: Nonreciprocal generation of Bell states via cooperative dissipation in a qubit-magnon system
papers.abstract: Directionally generating and controlling quantum states is critical in chiral quantum technologies. Here, we propose a scheme for the nonreciprocal generation of Bell states via cooperative dissipation in a qubit-magnon system, consisting of a superconducting transmon qubit and a yttrium iron garnet sphere subject to a bias magnetic field. The cooperative dissipation between them is induced by coupling both to a common transmission-line waveguide. Due to this cooperative dissipation, the system possesses a dark eigenstate within the single-excitation subspace. Under appropriate parameter conditions, the dark eigenstate reduces to a specific Bell state. With the assistance of a drive pulse, the system can be prepared in this Bell state (i.e., the dark eigenstate). In particular, we find that the dark eigenstate corresponds to different Bell states under positive ($+\mathbf{B}_0$) and negative ($-\mathbf{B}_0$) bias fields. Consequently, nonreciprocal Bell-state generation is achieved: $+\mathbf{B}_0$ yields one Bell state, while $-\mathbf{B}_0$ yields the other. Moreover, we define a fidelity-based nonreciprocal rate to quantify this nonreciprocity. Our work establishes cooperative dissipation as a versatile resource for nonreciprocal entangled-state generation, opening a promising route toward chiral quantum technologies.

papers.title: Majorization for superpositions of nonorthogonal states and the existence of golden states
papers.abstract: Golden states, from which every state can be prepared by free operations, are the units of a resource theory. In the resource theory of superposition relative to linearly independent, nonorthogonal reference states, they were known only for two reference states and for special overlap matrices, all of them maximally coherent in the Löwdin basis. We determine what decides their existence and when this Löwdin pattern holds. For every overlap matrix, the robustness and the geometric measure of superposition are maximized by the same states, which overlap equally with all reference states; the maximal values are set by the ground-state energy of a classical $XY$ model on the dual basis. These states, and only these, are golden under the maximal superposition-free operations, but they need not be maximally coherent in the Löwdin basis. For the Kraus-type free operations, we prove Gram majorization, a necessary and sufficient criterion for converting pure states into targets with nonzero coefficients, which reduces to majorization for orthonormal reference states. It shows that every golden state of these operations is maximally coherent in the Löwdin basis, yet golden states exist only for special overlap matrices: three reference states that are not orthonormal admit one if and only if their overlaps have a common modulus $s$ and their Bargmann phase $Φ$ obeys $s\geq2\cos[(π+|Φ|)/3]$, so that a geometric phase decides whether the theory has a unit. Finally, equal-overlap states yield a complete family of superposition witnesses in the Löwdin basis, which show that white noise is a resource unless the reference states are orthonormal.

papers.title: Fluid Antenna Array-Enabled Near-Field ISAC: Joint Port Position Optimization and Transmit Beamforming Design
papers.abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) have shown that activating a single port from a densely packed antenna array can yield spatial diversity comparable to that of tens of independent antennas, a property that has substantially improved communication reliability and efficiency. The fluid antenna array (FAA) extends this concept to multi-port configurations while avoiding complex multi-dimensional spatial correlation, and offers significant geometrical flexibility under a finite aperture and a limited port budget. These attributes motivate environment-adaptive array geometry for sensing in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Although this flexibility enables adaptive array geometries that exploit near-field distance-angle information, improving multi-parameter target estimation under communication and deployment constraints remains challenging. In this paper, we propose a planar FAA-assisted near-field ISAC framework for multiuser communication and target sensing. Specifically, we derive the Fisher information matrix (FIM) and the corresponding Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for the joint estimation of target range, zenith angle, azimuth angle, and radial velocity. Based on the derived CRB, we jointly optimize the FAA port positions and transmit beamforming to improve sensing accuracy while satisfying communication signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), transmit power, and physical deployment constraints. To solve the resulting non-convex problem, we develop a two-stage alternating optimization algorithm, in which transmit beamforming is optimized through semidefinite relaxation (SDR), while FAA port positions are successively optimized through discrete search and continuous refinement. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm achieves favorable sensing performance while maintaining a reasonable computational cost.

papers.title: Equilibria of Replicator Dynamics in Quantum Games
papers.abstract: We analyse two-population replicator dynamics for asymmetric $2\times2$ games implemented with the Marinatto--Weber (MW) identity/bit-flip protocol. The effective payoff matrices are explicit convex combinations of relabelled classical matrices. Consequently, the dynamics depends on the initial state only through its four computational-basis probabilities: quantum phases, coherences and entanglement cannot be distinguished from classical shared randomness by the payoffs or trajectories in this protocol. At each pure-strategy vertex, the local eigenvalues equal the negatives of the corresponding unilateral payoff advantages; a vertex is asymptotically stable precisely when it is a strict Nash equilibrium, and thus an evolutionarily stable strategy pair in the asymmetric-game sense. Explicit examples show how varying the initial distribution changes which vertex is stable. When an isolated interior rest point exists, it is a saddle or a nonlinear centre according to the sign of the product of the classical payoff cross-differences; the sign cannot change under the MW mapping, although the point can enter or leave the strategy square. We give all four vertex-stability conditions explicitly in a single table, obtain a closed-form logistic solution on the parity-balanced hyperplane $S=0$, classify the degenerate cases, and give a first integral for the nondegenerate flow. All results concern the MW payoff protocol and its classically simulable family of bimatrix games; none constitutes evidence of an inherently quantum evolutionary advantage.

papers.title: Needle-beam generation from SPDC photons using inverse-designed flat optics
papers.abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the generation of needle-like beams from spontaneous parametric downconversion (SPDC) light using a compact inverse-designed multilevel diffractive lens (MDL). The nonclassical nature of the SPDC source is independently verified through a three-detector heralded Hanbury Brown-Twiss measurement performed before the MDL, yielding a zero-delay second-order correlation value of approximately 0.14. Spatial measurements using an intensified charge-coupled device reveal that the MDL maintains a tightly confined focal distribution over an axial distance of approximately 11 mm under collinear SPDC illumination, substantially reducing diffraction-induced broadening compared with a conventional plano-convex lens of the same nominal focal length. Under non-collinear SPDC illumination, two distinct regions of extended axial confinement are observed, demonstrating the dependence of the engineered focal distribution on the incident spatial field. These results establish a compact flat-optical approach for engineering extended-focus SPDC photon fields, with potential applications in structured quantum photonics.
